newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sugar, soymeal ships hit by Santos strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sugar, soymeal ships hit by Santos strike.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Santos was partially paralyzed by an indefinite strike involving a group of administrative workers which began at 0100 local/0400 GMT today, a CODESP port authority spokesman said.
Of the 37 ships docked in the port, 11 ships are operating, five of which are loading liquids in public terminals and six in private terminals.
Some 23 ships docked in CODESP berths have been hit by the strike, including eight ships loading bagged sugar, one loading bulk sugar and one loading soymeal, CODESP said.
The strike involves around 800 of 2,000 members of the Administrative Portworkers' Union who are protesting a switch to 24-hour operations at the port, the spokesman said.

Santos port authority earlier this month announced it would switch to operating 24 hours a day as of 1900 local/2200 GMT on June 30 allowing a faster transit of cargoes and creating cost savings for users.
The administrative union said that although it agreed with the measure in principle, it was protesting against Codesp's failure to discuss the plan with its members.
Round table talks are being held today at the local Labor Tribunal in Santos but the stoppage was likely to continue at least throughout the day, the port spokesman said.
The workers involved in the strike are responsible for monitoring loading and unloading of vessels as well as providing technical assistance, he added.
All warehouse activities have also been paralysed by the stoppage, CODESP said.
